description: DynamicValue Apache Arrow IPC byte-lock, SINGLE-RUNTIME (.NET only — see SCOPE at the end of this description) (Arrow Phase 2, option c). SHREDDED NODE-TABLE: one RecordBatch, one row per tree node in DFS pre-order. Columns: kind Int8 (0=Null 1=Bool 2=Int 3=Float 4=String 5=Bytes 6=Array 7=Object), parent Int32 (-1 root), key Utf8?, b Bool?, i Int64?, f Float64?, s Utf8?, by Binary?. arrowHex = lowercase hex of ToArrow(value). SCOPE — READ BEFORE CITING THIS FILE AS CROSS-LANGUAGE EVIDENCE: F# (Zeta.Core.DynamicValueArrow.toArrow) and C# (DynamicValuesArrow.ToArrow) both call the SAME .NET Apache.Arrow library and emit BYTE-IDENTICAL IPC, so their agreement is agreement between perfectly correlated implementations and is not independent evidence. This is a ROUND-TRIP / same-library check, NOT a cross-implementation one: it pins that our two .NET call sites stay byte-stable, and says NOTHING about whether pyarrow, arrow-rs or arrow-cpp can read these bytes. Closing that gap needs a vector produced by a non-.NET Arrow implementation, checked in hex-in-JSON per the no-binary-in-the-proof-lineage rule; that is NOT done here. Value set mirrors golden-vectors-xml.json. Never-collapse free: Null, empty arr, empty obj, empty str, empty bytes are distinct kind tags. Float preserves the exact IEEE-754 bits (NaN/-0.0/Inf/subnormals).
